links.outcome: Answer quality of retrieval- and search-grounded agent versus plain LLM on high-complexity questions
links.effect: Embedding average score on high-complexity questions was 82.849 for AI agents vs 77.825 for LLMs; agents were particularly effective in clinical consultation tasks.
links.quote: Using a dual-evaluation framework comprising automated metrics and expert manual assessments, our results demonstrated that AI agents substantially outperformed LLMs in addressing high-complexity questions (embedding average score: 82.849 for AI agents vs 77.825 for LLMs) and were particularly effective in clinical consultation tasks.

links.outcome: Output variability across 30 repeated runs of the agent
links.effect: Mean absolute deviation of 0.0167 (embedding average score) and 0.0387 (BERTScore) after 30 repeated experiments, indicating stable, minimally variable responses.
links.quote: After 30 repeated experiments, the mean absolute deviation of the AI agents in the embedding average score and BERTScore metrics were 0.0167 and 0.0387, respectively.

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks an AI agent architecture combining LLMs, RAG, and search engine tools against standard LLMs using retrospective patient questions; it evaluates the novel system rather than a deployment practice/safeguard applied to an existing tool.
